answer_text:
We integrate

\[
f(z)=\frac{e^{iz}}{z}
\]

over the standard indented upper-half-plane contour of radii \(R\) and \(\varepsilon\).

Let \(C_{R,\varepsilon}\) be the positively oriented boundary of

\[
\{z:\varepsilon<|z|<R,\ \operatorname{Im}z>0\}.
\]

Its pieces are:

- the line segment from \(\varepsilon\) to \(R\) on the real axis,
- the outer semicircle \(C_R: z=Re^{i\theta}\), \(0\le \theta\le \pi\),
- the line segment from \(-R\) to \(-\varepsilon\),
- the inner semicircle \(C_\varepsilon: z=\varepsilon e^{i\theta}\), \(\pi\ge\theta\ge 0\) (clockwise).

Since \(f\) is analytic in this region, Cauchy’s theorem gives

\[
\int_{\varepsilon}^{R}\frac{e^{ix}}{x}\,dx
+\int_{C_R}\frac{e^{iz}}{z}\,dz
+\int_{-R}^{-\varepsilon}\frac{e^{ix}}{x}\,dx
+\int_{C_\varepsilon}\frac{e^{iz}}{z}\,dz
=0.
\]

Now estimate each part.

For the outer semicircle,

\[
\left|\int_{C_R}\frac{e^{iz}}{z}\,dz\right|
\le \int_0^\pi e^{-R\sin\theta}\,d\theta \to 0
\qquad (R\to\infty).
\]

For the inner semicircle, with \(z=\varepsilon e^{i\theta}\),

\[
\int_{C_\varepsilon}\frac{e^{iz}}{z}\,dz
=
i\int_{\pi}^{0} e^{i\varepsilon e^{i\theta}}\,d\theta
=
-i\int_0^\pi e^{i\varepsilon e^{i\theta}}\,d\theta
\to -i\pi
\qquad (\varepsilon\to 0).
\]

For the real-axis parts,

\[
\int_{-R}^{-\varepsilon}\frac{e^{ix}}{x}\,dx
=
-\int_{\varepsilon}^{R}\frac{e^{-ix}}{x}\,dx,
\]

so

\[
\int_{\varepsilon}^{R}\frac{e^{ix}}{x}\,dx
+
\int_{-R}^{-\varepsilon}\frac{e^{ix}}{x}\,dx
=
\int_{\varepsilon}^{R}\frac{e^{ix}-e^{-ix}}{x}\,dx
=
2i\int_{\varepsilon}^{R}\frac{\sin x}{x}\,dx.
\]

Letting \(R\to\infty\) and \(\varepsilon\to 0\),

\[
0=0-i\pi+2i\int_0^\infty \frac{\sin x}{x}\,dx.
\]

Hence

\[
2i\int_0^\infty \frac{\sin x}{x}\,dx=i\pi,
\]

so

\[
\int_0^\infty \frac{\sin x}{x}\,dx=\frac{\pi}{2}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{\pi}{2}}
\]
